question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting decimal-equivalent spellings such as `+500` and `0500`, or should the Policy CLI adopt a canonical digits-only input contract that breaks those existing invocations?
rationale: Current code and shipped behavior accept these spellings, while public docs define the numeric interval but not its canonical textual representation; removing accepted inputs is a Policy-owner compatibility decision.

options.title: Preserve accepted spellings
options.body: Keep the existing numeric contract because the aliases resolve to the same cadence and no documented bug or canonical lexical requirement is established.

options.title: Approve canonical digits only
options.body: Accept the compatibility break only with explicit Policy-owner approval, public documentation, concise invariant-focused code, and supported-Node before/after/control CLI proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve accepted spellings
recommendation.body: Keep the existing numeric contract because the aliases resolve to the same cadence and no documented bug or canonical lexical requirement is established.

likelyOwner.reason: The original and most sustained merged history for the Policy CLI and its conformance behavior points to this person.
